description: We’re BLIVIX ASTRO, a team of students passionate about space, AI, data, and technology. We enjoy turning ideas into practical, creative solutions using NASA’s open data.
summary:
Space Disaster System is an intelligent multi-hazard monitoring platform designed to help people explore and understand natural disasters using publicly available Earth observation and environmental data.

The platform integrates NASA FIRMS satellite-based fire detection data with earthquake information from USGS, weather information from Open-Meteo, and disaster-related information to provide a unified view of multiple hazards, including wildfires, earthquakes, cyclones, and weather conditions.

Through an interactive dashboard and geographical visualization, users can explore disaster events, monitor environmental conditions, and access information from multiple data sources in one place.

By simplifying access to complex environmental information, Space Disaster System aims to improve disaster awareness, support preparedness, and demonstrate how satellite observations and technology can contribute to community resilience.
details:
Project Overview

Space Disaster System is a multi-hazard monitoring and disaster intelligence platform that brings different environmental and disaster-related data sources together into a single interactive dashboard.

How It Works

The platform collects and processes information from multiple sources:

  • NASA FIRMS: Satellite-based active fire and thermal anomaly detections.
  • USGS: Earthquake event information.
  • Open-Meteo: Weather conditions and forecasts.
  • GDACS: Disaster-related information and global event monitoring.

The backend provides dedicated APIs for fire events, earthquakes, cyclones, weather conditions, and combined disaster information. The frontend presents the information through an interactive dashboard and geographical visualizations.

Key Features

  • Multi-hazard monitoring through a unified dashboard.
  • Satellite-based wildfire detection.
  • Earthquake event visualization.
  • Weather monitoring using location-based data.
  • Disaster information sections.
  • Interactive geographical visualization.
  • Centralized access to information from multiple data providers.

Technologies Used

  • Python and Flask for backend development.
  • HTML, CSS and JavaScript for frontend development.
  • REST APIs for data integration.
  • NASA FIRMS for satellite fire detection data.
  • USGS Earthquake API.
  • Open-Meteo Weather API.
  • GDACS disaster information.
  • Interactive map-based visualization.

Innovation and Impact

The project's innovation lies in integrating multiple disaster-related data sources into one accessible platform rather than requiring users to visit separate websites.

It aims to improve disaster awareness, simplify access to environmental information, and support preparedness and informed decision-making.

Future Scope

Future improvements include advanced predictive analytics, automated disaster alerts, machine-learning-based risk assessment, enhanced cyclone tracking, and expanded satellite data integration.
